title: The Case of the Missing Kenkey

pages.text: Detective Sitsofe put on her detective hat. Her little brother Selase held his torch. “Case number one,” said Sitsofe. “Someone has taken the kenkey from the kitchen!” “It was on the table,” said Selase. “And now it is gone!”
sentences: Detective Sitsofe put on her detective hat.
Her little brother Selase held his torch.
“Case number one,” said Sitsofe.
“Someone has taken the kenkey from the kitchen!” “It was on the table,” said Selase.
“And now it is gone!”
pages.alt: A girl in a detective hat and her little brother with a torch look at an empty table.

pages.text: “First, we look for clues,” said Sitsofe. She looked at the floor. “Footprints!” They were small and round, with four toes. “They are not our feet,” said Selase. “Four toes on each print,” said Sitsofe. “Hmm. Who has four toes?”
sentences: “First, we look for clues,” said Sitsofe.
She looked at the floor.
“Footprints!” They were small and round, with four toes.
“They are not our feet,” said Selase.
“Four toes on each print,” said Sitsofe.
“Hmm.
Who has four toes?”
pages.alt: A girl with a magnifying glass looks at small round footprints on the floor.

pages.text: Next, Sitsofe found a crumb on the stool. Then another crumb on the floor. A trail of crumbs led towards the back door. “The thief walked this way,” she said. Selase tiptoed along the crumbs, shining his torch.
sentences: Next, Sitsofe found a crumb on the stool.
Then another crumb on the floor.
A trail of crumbs led towards the back door.
“The thief walked this way,” she said.
Selase tiptoed along the crumbs, shining his torch.
pages.alt: A trail of crumbs leads across the kitchen floor to the back door.

pages.text: At the back door, Sitsofe sniffed. “I can smell kenkey,” she said. “And something else… something furry.” Selase giggled. “Maybe it is a giant rat!” “Or a cat,” said Sitsofe. “We need to look more closely.”
sentences: At the back door, Sitsofe sniffed.
“I can smell kenkey,” she said.
“And something else… something furry.” Selase giggled.
“Maybe it is a giant rat!” “Or a cat,” said Sitsofe.
“We need to look more closely.”
pages.alt: A girl and boy sniff near the back door of a kitchen.

pages.text: They opened the back door. Under the bush sat a small brown puppy with floppy ears. Biscuit had crumbs on his nose and a very full tummy. He wagged his tail. “Woof!” “Biscuit!” gasped Selase. “The thief!”
sentences: They opened the back door.
Under the bush sat a small brown puppy with floppy ears.
Biscuit had crumbs on his nose and a very full tummy.
He wagged his tail.
“Woof!” “Biscuit!” gasped Selase.
“The thief!”
pages.alt: A puppy with crumbs on its nose sits under a bush.

pages.text: “But wait,” said Sitsofe. “A puppy cannot climb on a table. Biscuit is too small. Someone must have helped him.” Selase went quiet. He twisted his toes. “Selase?” said Sitsofe. “Did you put the kenkey on the floor for Biscuit?”
sentences: “But wait,” said Sitsofe.
“A puppy cannot climb on a table.
Biscuit is too small.
Someone must have helped him.” Selase went quiet.
He twisted his toes.
“Selase?” said Sitsofe.
“Did you put the kenkey on the floor for Biscuit?”
pages.alt: A small boy looks down at his feet while his sister watches.

pages.text: Selase nodded. “He looked so hungry,” he said in a small voice. “I am sorry. I should have asked first.” Sitsofe hugged him. “Thank you for telling the truth,” she said. “That is what a good detective does, even when the clue points at yourself.”

pages.alt: A girl hugs her little brother in the kitchen doorway.

pages.text: Just then, Auntie Ekua came in with a plate. “I heard everything,” she laughed. “Next time, ask first. And Biscuit has his own dinner.” She gave Biscuit a bowl of puppy food and Sitsofe and Selase a fresh piece of kenkey to share. “Case closed,” said Sitsofe. The end.
